For Applicant - Mr. Sumit Singh, Advocate.
For State/non-applicant - Mr. Jitendra Shukla, Panel Lawyer.
 Hon'ble Shri Justice Rakesh Mohan Pandey

Order on Board
16-02-2023
1.
With the consent of the parties, the matter is heard finally.

2. This application has been filed under Section 438 of the Cr.P.C. for grant of anticipatory bail in
connection with Crime No.122/2022 registered at Police Station Mahila Thana Durg, District Durg,
Chhattisgarh for offence punishable under Section 498A read with Section 34 of the Ipc.
3. As per the prosecution story, the applicant and the complainant were married on 25-10-2019.

The allegation against the present applicant is that after marriage; he harassed the complainant; took some objectionable videos and photographs and compelled her to make physical relation with other persons.
It is further alleged that she never made complaint to save her married life.
It is also stated that, she was brutally assaulted by the present applicant many times and he has taken Rs.25,00,000/- from her in installments.
The complainant has also stated in the written complaint that, she is a Doctor and she has sufficient means of income whereas allegations against other co- accused persons are general in nature.

On such complaint police registered FIR for offence punishable under Section 498A read with Section 34 of the IPC against the present applicant and mother-in-law, brother-in-law and sister-in-law of the complainant.

4. Learned counsel for the applicant would submit that at present applicant is posted as Nayak in Indian Army and false allegations have been made against him because most of the time, the applicant stays at posted place.
He would further submit that the complainant is a Doctor and she wants to get rid from the present applicant, therefore, she has made false allegations against him and his family members.
He would pray for grant of anticipatory bail to the applicant.

sentences.text: 5. On the other hand, learned counsel for the State would oppose and submit that there are serious allegations against the present applicant.
6. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the case diary.

7. From the case diary it appears that on 25-10-2019 marriage was solemnized between the applicant and the complainant and after three years the FIR has been lodged against the present applicant and other co-accused persons.
Undisputedly, the complainant is a Doctor and present applicant is posted as Nayak in Indian Army and presently he is posted in Kashmir.
The FIR reflects that marriage with the applicant was third marriage of complainant and after three years FIR has been lodged.

Considering the fact that the applicant is posted as Nayak in Indian Army and at presently he is posted in Kashmir, there are general allegations against all the accused persons and other co-accused persons have already been extended benefit of anticipatory bail
, I am inclined to allow this application.

8. Accordingly, the anticipatory bail application is allowed and it is ordered that in the event of arrest of the applicant in connection with aforesaid offence, he shall be released on anticipatory bail by the officer arresting him on his executing a personal bond of Rs.50,000/- to the satisfaction of the officer arresting him.

(iii) that he shall not act in any manner which will be prejudicial to fair and expeditious trial; and (iv) that he shall appear before the trial Court on each and every date given to him by the said Court till disposal of the trial.
9. The observation made in the course of this order are only for considering the case of applicant on the application for grant of anticipatory bail.
The concerned trial Court shall not be influenced or bound by the observation made in the course of this order.
